text:
mike: Seeing a spike of TLS handshake failures for a handful of custom domains in eu-west-1 since ~08:00 UTC. Customers report browser errors showing our wildcard cert instead of their custom cert.

anita: Any recent infra or ingress deploys around that time? :thinking_face:

mike: No platform deploys. Checked autoscaling and node events — nothing. Grabbed ALB access logs: a lot of requests are matching the default listener rule (no Host header match) -> default cert served.

sara: Are we using ALB ingress controller or TCP passthrough? If ALB and host rules are missing, ALB will return the default cert. Also remember ALB picks rule via SNI during TLS handshake.

mike: We're on aws-alb-ingress-controller. Ingress annotations look standard:

```
# snippets from the ingress annotation
alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/scheme: internet-facing
alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/listen-ports: '[{"HTTP":80},{"HTTPS":443}]'
service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: HTTPS
```

But when I compared manifests vs live rules I found customer-c domains missing from the ingress spec (they were removed somehow).

chris: Could be k8s apply/helm truncation or a chart templating bug. Did the controller log any reconcile errors?

mike: Controller logs show a successful reconcile, but when I `aws elbv2 describe-rules` the listener has a wildcard rule with higher precedence than the specific host for customer-c — effectively crowding it out. The specific host rule exists but got a lower priority number. ALB matched wildcard and returned the wildcard cert.

anita: How did priorities get scrambled? We normally let the controller pick priorities. Any manual priority annotations or hardcoded values in a chart?

mike: Found an ingress created by an experimental service that used a hardcoded annotation `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/priority: "200"`. The controller during reconciliation tried to honor it and then compacted priorities, pushing a specific customer rule below the wildcard. Priority collisions -> rule order changed.

sara: That's nasty. Also remember some clients (old embedded libcurl or certain mobile carriers) don't send SNI; those will always hit default cert regardless of rules. Is the failure cohort all non-SNI clients?

mike: Mostly EU mobile ranges and some embedded devices, but we also saw desktop browsers intermittently, which aligns with the priority shuffle theory rather than pure SNI absence.

chris: Immediate mitigation options:
- Re-order listener rules so customer-specific hosts have higher precedence (manual, fast).
- Remove/lock wildcard rules while we fix chart/controller logic.
- Short-term: add explicit priority annotations on critical customer ingresses with a high number (so they win).

anita: For long-term: patch the ingress-controller reconciliation to allocate priorities deterministically (avoid honoring arbitrary hardcoded priorities from charts without validation). Add CI checks to the helm charts preventing reused low values.

mike: I applied a manual re-order to the listener and validated with curl using --resolve:

```
$ curl -v --resolve customer-c.example.com:443:ALB_IP https://customer-c.example.com/
* Connected to ALB_IP (ALB_IP) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshake completed
*  subject: CN=customer-c.example.com
*  server certificate verified
```
Customer-c now sees correct cert. I also patched the ingress manifest to set `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/priority: \"1000\"` for the critical hosts as an emergency guard.

deploy-bot: Certificate rotation for *.redwood-inference.com completed 09:12 UTC :white_check_mark:

chris: Follow-ups: (1) Audit controller reconciliation logs to find where hardcoded priorities are accepted, (2) add unit/integration tests to avoid priority collisions, (3) update helm charts to disallow static low-number priorities, (4) plan migration for customers needing mTLS/TLS passthrough to NLB where SNI is forwarded.

anita: I'll open a PR for the controller fix and a hotfix for the helm chart rule lint.

mike: I'll keep a watch on ALB access logs and CloudWatch metrics for the next 6 hours and escalate if anything reappears. Leaving a note in the incident tracker too. :lock: 

sara: Good catch. Post the PR and a short incident summary when done so CS can notify affected customers.

chris: Also consider adding an automated rule audit job that alerts when wildcard rules precede specific host rules in any listener. That would detect regressions quickly.

mike: Agree. Adding that to the infra backlog.
